summary: The University of Glasgow's African Excellence Award takes 75% off the tuition fee of a one-year taught master's in any subject, starting in September 2027. Up to 16 awards go to students who live in Africa, hold an African passport and have grades equivalent to a UK First Class degree. The deadline is 31 March 2027.
meta_title: Glasgow African Excellence Award 2027: 75% tuition waiver
meta_description: Glasgow's African Excellence Award takes 75% off a one-year taught master's for up to 16 African students with First Class grades. Apply by 31 March 2027.
covers: 75% of your tuition fee for a one-year taught master's. On an Arts and Humanities programme Glasgow puts this at £20,542.50; the value depends on your fee.
eligibility: Living in Africa and holding a passport from one of the 54 eligible African countries and regions, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa among them.
Grades equivalent to a UK First Class honours degree.
A place, or an application, for a one-year full-time taught master's starting in September 2027, in any discipline. PG Diplomas and PG Certificates are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible one-year taught master's for September 2027. You do not need an offer to apply for the award, but you need one to be invited to interview.
Complete the award application, which asks for a clear career and development plan.
Shortlisted applicants are invited to interview by 7 May 2027.
watch_out: The award covers tuition only. You still need the living costs the UK visa rules require.
Glasgow scholarships and discounts cannot be combined with each other or with outside sponsorship, except the Alumni Discount. If you are offered two, the smaller one is removed.
Up to 16 awards across the whole university, so apply for other funding too.

faq.q: How much is the Glasgow African Excellence Award worth?
faq.a: 75% of the tuition fee of a one-year taught master's. Glasgow gives £20,542.50 as the value on an Arts and Humanities programme.
Yes. Ghana is on the list of eligible African countries; you must also live in Africa and have International fee status.
31 March 2027 at 23:59 UK time, for courses starting in September 2027.
